long_biography.plain_text:
Building his first purpose-made steel passenger vessel moved Marijo Ercegović from operating excursion craft towards creating a charter fleet of his own. The Croatian captain combined vessel development with weekly coastal itineraries, giving him control over both the operating platform and the guest experience.

Ercegović had already spent years at sea, first on sand-extraction ships and then as a fisherman with three boats. He entered tourism with an excursion service in 1998 and subsequently established round-trip charters along the Dalmatian coast. That hands-on progression from working captain to builder-owner helped establish a family-run Croatian small-ship charter business.

uncertainties.detail: A different Marijo Ercegović of Jesenice was born in 1958 and died in 2015. He was excluded because the owner is a living captain born in 1963, identified on a current first-party site and in a continuous business chronology corroborated by Croatian ministry records.
The canonical Croatian surname Ercegović is preserved. ASCII Ercegovic searches were used only for discovery and did not produce a competing business identity.

Public sources describe a long family maritime tradition and family involvement in the operating business, but they do not establish every individual's ownership or relationship. No role is inferred for Andrija, Zdenka or other Ercegović family members from surname alone.

Ercegović's family background supplied meaningful maritime exposure, but no public source establishes that he inherited the controlling business or its capital. Self-made — advantaged start therefore captures the evidence more accurately than Inherited and expanded or a fully independent start.

The 1963 birth year is supported by an exact-name specialist profile and corroborating charter-distribution record. The day and month appear only in syndicated commercial crew listings and are withheld from proposals, while no reliable public source establishes his birthplace or birth country.

Current sources establish continued ownership and operation in passenger excursions and charter tourism, but the full private-company structure and ownership percentages are not publicly documented. No valuation, revenue or net-worth claim is included.

No personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website could be verified to the exact-name captain at the required confidence. The first-party charter site was used as identity evidence rather than proposed as a personal or general company social link.
